files.doc:
Fails (exit 1) when the teaching layer is missing an explanation (ADR-0003):
- a dependency of any project that no tool card covers
- an ADR of any project without a decision card (and decision cards for ADRs that don't exist)
- journey links to decisions or concepts that don't exist; glossary links to missing concepts
- a decision card whose `chosen` index points outside its options
Run with `npm run coverage` (CI runs it on every PR).

Reads a TypeScript/JavaScript/Astro codebase into code facts (same shape as read_python.py).
node scripts/read-typescript.mjs <repo_dir> <out.json>
Uses the TypeScript compiler's parser (no type-checking, no execution). Records functions,
React components, classes and types with their parameters, defaults and doc comments, plus
calls and JSX component uses it can resolve with certainty (same file or relative imports).

Imports the "records" (ADRs, devlogs, roadmap, status) and the facts (dependencies, CI jobs,
history) of every project in sources.config.json. Run with `npm run sync`.
Why: the site must never disagree with the projects it teaches. Records are copied, not
retyped, and facts are read from the projects' own files (ADR-0002, ADR-0003).
Output is deterministic (no timestamps), so a sync that changes nothing produces no diff.

The content model (ADR-0002). Every teaching entry has a fixed shape, checked at build
time: a concept without a "why" or a decision without options fails the build, the same
way a type error fails a program.

Finds acronyms in text and decides where to spell them out. Shared by the page plugin
(rehype-acronyms.mjs) and the interactive components (Inline.tsx), so both behave the same.
The site's areas: one per project, plus the shared "Combined knowledge".

Build-time plugin for every Markdown/MDX page, including imported records:
wraps acronyms in <abbr title="full form"> and spells out the first use on each page.

Shared helpers for components.
A link inside the site that respects the GitHub Pages base path.

Scoped navigation: inside a project you see only that project; the shared material lives in
"Combined knowledge". The full sidebar is defined once in astro.config.mjs; this middleware
keeps only the current area's group, and limits previous/next links to that area.

Every project has the same sections, grouped the way an architect reads a system:
 understand it → look inside the code → see the decisions → learn from its history.

walkthroughs and the build's snippet checks. Python is read with Python's own parser.

Picks live in this browser only (ADR-0005). Storage can be unavailable (private mode,
blocked site data), so every access is guarded and the page works without it.
